//: The uniqueness guarantees a restore must preserve.
A count comparison cannot see these. `mongorestore` exits 0 whether or not it restored
the indexes, and a dump taken with `--noIndexRestore`, or one restored that way, comes
back with every document and none of the constraints — so two rows sharing a
`riskAssessmentId` would be accepted by a database that is supposed to forbid it. The
restore script verifies this list after every restore, and the backup/restore drill
creates exactly this list so the verification has something to find.
These are the unique indexes `MongoStore.ensureIndexes()` creates. That is asserted in
both directions against a real MongoDB by
`apps/api/test/release/critical-indexes.test.ts`: every entry here must exist on the
real store, and the store must not create a unique index this list omits. Without the
second direction a new uniqueness guarantee could be added and never verified after a
